text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt and Spain agree to increase investments through cooperation of businesspeople. King Juan Carlos of Spain tells a business encounter that Egypt is witnessing an economic revival that will open new horizons. Cooperation in the fields of tourism, industry, telecommunications and trade.
- Spain considers giving Egypt loans worth $300 million over three years.
- President Hosni Mubarak discusses bilateral ties with foreign minister of Kyrgyzstan.
- Mubarak discusses terrorism and the future of Jerusalem with members of an international Islamic forum.

- President meets members of the Call for Islam international forum, discusses issues of Islamic world and Jerusalem. Former Sudanese president Suwar el-Dahab says Israel is trying to infiltrate Africa and take control of it.
- Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad hold telephone discussion on bilateral issues and Middle East peace.
- Radio Israel says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Egypt next month.
- Dangerous Israeli provocations in Israel. Netanyahu repeats his government's insistence to build (Jewish neighbourhoods) throughout the city.
- World Bank agency to protect Egyptian investments abroad and insure international investments in Egypt.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says European investments in Egypt amounted to $23 billion. Egypt and Spain signed a protocol with Spain to encourage investment and support development.
- Prosecutor still detaining the four leaders of the Satanists group but releases the remaining suspects.
